abstract: We construct dihedral switch preparations for the ordinary no-three-in-line problem with changing occupied support, four conserved projections, and full leading local capacity. For each fixed $0<\theta<1$, arbitrarily large even $N$ admit $(1-\theta)N/2-o(N)$ direct blocks and $\theta N/16-o(N)$ occupancy packets. Each packet has exactly 258 maximum quarter-turn-invariant states of 32 points. Every global choice has $2N-o(N)$ points, is clean in a growing set of short directions, has no one- or two-unit triple, and has capacity at most three on remaining lines. The three-unit interaction hypergraph can have Berge girth tending to infinity. A twisted Young convolution estimate removes every fixed cycle length at negligible cost; an integer-divisibility count leaves one complementary chirality predicate on each all-direct edge. Resource coloring mixes the two families with finite-order spread constants uniform in the direction cutoff. Against a fixed clean quarter-turn-invariant exterior, we determine the exact largest compatible packet subset, even allowing asymmetric subsets. We also prove completion against three forbidden sites, localize one-unit exterior repairs, and give a sparse neutral-donor construction. Six standalone integer controls accompany the analytic proofs. The matching input, concentration inequality, tomography operations and general cycle-alteration method are credited to prior work. Global compatibility remains unresolved: neither high girth nor the local state count establishes a clean near-density-two choice or an unrestricted lower bound above $1.8N$.

coauthors.contribution: Clean occupancy convolution; three-pin completion; target-dependent donor localization; sparse neutral-donor construction; shared-pair interaction pruning and direct-edge divisor count; independent analytic audits of transfers, exact response and twisted high-girth pruning; final manuscript review.

title: Dihedral switch preparations with high-girth interactions and exact exterior response
